title: Nonendoscopic Detection of Barrett's Esophagus on Patients Without Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Symptoms.
abstract: Upper endoscopy (EGD) is generally recommended in those with chronic gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). To evaluate nonendoscopic screening in those without GERD symptoms. EsoCheck/Esoguard (LucidDx) was performed in recruited patients without chronic GERD who had ≥3 other BE risk factors. The EsoGuard assay was positive in 34 of 120 patients. BE was identified in 9 of 27 who had follow-up EGD, positive predictive value = 33% (17%-54%). EGD performed in 22 of 86 subjects with negative assays found no BE, negative predictive value = 100% (85%-100%). Nonendoscopic BE detection is effective in patients without chronic GERD.
